brief.headline: Close a ₹8.48 L/year price gap by matching the ₹7.62/NOS bottle price we already pay elsewhere, then qualify Manjushree or Mold-Tek as a second source.

priceAsk.summary: Match the ₹7.62/NOS price we pay TPAC for the same 250ml amber PET bottle, cutting their ₹8.49 to close the gap.
priceAsk.target: ₹7.62/NOS on the PET BOT AMBER 250ML/28MM WITH SHR SL 01 (saves ₹8.48 L/year across the basket)
priceAsk.basis: We already buy this exact bottle type from TPAC Packaging at ₹7.62/NOS — an 11.5% lower price. The market reference (₹0.85–0.95/pc for 28mm PP caps) says MARKET-FAIR with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume, so our ₹7.62 bottle benchmark is defensible. The ₹8.48 L annual excess is the cost of staying at their price.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep 30 Days After Receipt as-is; it already frees up ₹15.75 L for us and is not our worst term.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹15.75 L cash freed up for us (already realized under the current 30-day arrangement)

brief.financialLeverage: PIK Plastics publishes no financial statements, so we cannot see their revenue, profit or cash position. Our ₹1.92 Cr annual spend is material but we have no way to gauge how big we are to them. Because their finances are opaque, the plan leans on our own purchase data — the ₹8.48 L gap vs. our best price — and on lining up a robust second source (Manjushree, Mold-Tek) to reduce single-supplier risk. Push firmly on price to the ₹7.62 benchmark, but keep the tone professional and factual since we lack the transparency to judge their room to move.

evidence.point: We pay PIK ₹8.49/NOS for the 250ml amber PET bottle but pay TPAC only ₹7.62/NOS for the same item
Closing that 11.5% gap saves us ₹7.19 L/year on that one SKU alone
Total annual excess we pay PIK across rigid packaging vs our cheapest prices
Our current 30-day payment term already frees up cash for us
Market reference for 28mm PP caps shows fair pricing with modest headroom at volume
evidence.figure: ₹0.55–1.20/pc ask band; typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc; verdict MARKET-FAIR with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd (private, ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100)
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter covering pharma bottles, caps and preforms — the top second-source candidate for our PET bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd (listed, ₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health B 73/100)
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader in pails, containers and pharma packaging — strong and profitable, a robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: IVL Dhunseri Petrochem Industries Private Limited (manufacturer, India-East)
alternates.why: A lead to qualify (verify before RFQ) — PET resin/preform manufacturer in the East, medium confidence from web research.

risks: PIK's financials are not public, so we cannot see if they are under cash stress or highly profitable — judge their response in the room and be ready to soften if supply continuity looks shaky.

The ₹8.48 L gap is real but hinges on a single large SKU (the ₹8.49 bottle); if PIK pushes back on that item's spec or lead-time vs TPAC, have the ₹5.38 vs ₹5.24 bottle gap (₹1.29 L) ready as a secondary target.
We have strong listed alternates (Manjushree, Mold-Tek) but none are qualified or priced yet — start their RFQ process now so PIK knows a second source is moving, not theoretical.

Market backups (Reliance, IVL Dhunseri, Chemco) are leads from public research, not audited suppliers — do not present them as approved sources in this meeting; use only the availableAlternates as credible options.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We've benchmarked your 250ml amber bottle at ₹8.49 against the ₹7.62 we pay TPAC for the identical item — let's work together to close that 11.5% gap and lock in a long-term partnership at a fair price for both sides.
